Help

Where to get help

Free helplines and reliable resources for when you are struggling or worried about someone.

If your life or someone else's is in danger right now, call your local emergency number (112 in the European Union, 999 in the UK, 911 in the US and Canada) or go to the nearest emergency department. Do not wait.

This page brings together reliable helplines and resources for when you are going through a hard time. Asking for help is not overreacting or being a nuisance: it is what we would do for any other health problem.

United Kingdom and Ireland

  • 116 123 · Samaritans. Free, 24 hours, for anyone who is struggling.
  • 111 · NHS 111 (England), for urgent health advice, including mental health in many areas.
  • 0808 2000 247 · National Domestic Abuse Helpline (England), free and 24 hours.

United States and Canada

  • 988 · Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. Call or text, free and 24 hours.
  • 1-800-799-7233 · National Domestic Violence Hotline (US).

Spain

  • 112 · Emergencies.
  • 024 · Suicidal behaviour helpline. For people with suicidal thoughts and those close to them. Free, confidential and 24 hours.
  • 016 · Violence against women. Free, 24 hours, in more than 50 languages, and it does not show on the phone bill. Also on WhatsApp at 600 000 016.
  • 900 20 20 10 · ANAR Foundation. For children, adolescents and families, including school bullying. Free and 24 hours.
  • 717 003 717 · Teléfono de la Esperanza. Listening and emotional support in a crisis.
  • 900 100 036 · Infocáncer (Spanish Association Against Cancer). Information and free psychological support for patients and families, 24 hours.

In Spain, the usual route to mental health care is through your family doctor, who can refer you to the local Mental Health Centre. In a crisis, go to a hospital emergency department or call 112.

Latin America

Some numbers change over time or only work in certain areas or with certain carriers. In an emergency, the emergency number is always the safest option.

Other countries

The international directory Find A Helpline lists free helplines in many countries, by topic.

If you want to help someone else

  • Ask them directly how they are and listen without judging. Asking about suicide does not cause it.
  • Do not promise to keep a secret if their life is at risk.
  • Go with them to get help or make the call together.
  • If the risk is immediate, do not leave them alone and call the emergency number.

Numbers checked in November 2026. If you find one that is out of date, please let us know. Psycholopedia is an information website and does not provide healthcare.
